narrative: A docs-heavy licensing PR whose LICENSE-NOTES/CHANGELOG/FORKS prose went through five review rounds. Most round-1 findings were the same claims fixed in one file but not its sibling (F5->FORKS.md) or a location the round-0 reviewer explicitly named and the fix skipped (F3->no-license section). Rounds 2 and 3 each contained a single finding against a sentence the previous fix either kept (F16) or introduced (F17). Round 4 mixed pre-existing count errors with drift from F10's heading expansion and F4's undercounted enumeration. The one pushback (F8) was correct and well evidenced with go mod why output.
guidance_observations: Each round of doc fixes created new count/quantifier errors ('two other GPL texts', 'either module', 'freetype and mysql'), so a post-fix pass checking every count word and enumeration against the doc's own sections would have saved rounds 2-4.
Fixes were scoped to the exact file and sentence quoted even when the reviewer named a sibling location, which turned single findings into multi-round chains.
Duplicate findings (F9/F11/F14, F7/F15, F19/F20) were consolidated into one edit each, which was efficient.

evidence: The agent confirmed in the generated SBOM: '"licenses": [{"license": {"name": "MIT AND Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception"}}]'. 24aa823 routes compound expressions to the CycloneDX expression arm, using whole-token operator matching instead of the suggested substring sniff. The agent later conceded (issue comment, item 3) that the parse-dont-validate claim was overstated because the function proves only 'which arm', not well-formed SPDX.
guidance_note: When introducing a new shape of value (a compound SPDX expression) into an existing field, trace every serializer that consumes the field and check that the output format has a distinct slot for that shape.

evidence: This duplicates F1: the same componentLicenses mis-serialization, fixed by the same 24aa823 licenseChoice mapping. The parse-dont-validate citation was later conceded as overstated.
This duplicates F1, anchored at native.go's compiler-rt entry. The verified post-fix artifact shows '"compiler-rt": [{"expression": ...}]' with 152 components on license.name.
This duplicates F1. The reviewer's alternative of splitting into two licenses was not taken; the expression arm is the spec-correct home for AND/WITH.
This duplicates F1: the same root cause and the same fix in 24aa823.

The embedded license's Legacy section says 'you may choose to use it under either license' (NCSA or MIT), which is an election, so adding an NCSA AND-arm would claim a grant not taken. The real gap was the unstated election, and the agent took the reviewer's own second option ('state in the note why the NCSA text is carried but not claimed').
guidance_note: When a bundled license text contains a dual-license election, record the election in the shipped note at the same time as choosing the expression.

evidence: The claim that the expression 'assert[s] the ported routines are uniformly Apache-2.0' overstates things, since the MIT arm covers the MIT-elected pre-relicense routines. The missing election note was real, and the agent implemented the reviewer's offered alternative of stating the MIT election in the note.

narrative: One automated round raised five duplicate findings on the compound SPDX expression landing in license.name, plus two on the unstated NCSA/MIT election. The agent fixed the serialization with a token-based discriminator and wire-level tests, and recorded the election in the shipped note rather than adding a false NCSA arm. While fixing it, the agent found that release-validate.yml pinned the old flat compiler-rt row. After the reviewer died on a 402, substitute local reviews (issue comments) found false statements in the ICU and musl notes that the agent had written without reading the bytes.
guidance_observations: The compound expression was introduced without tracing its consumers (SBOM serializer, release-validate grep), so both breaks surfaced only through review.

Notes asserting facts about third-party license files were written from grep proximity rather than reading the text (the 'three GPL blocks' including MIT install-sh, and musl 'reproduces every notice verbatim'), and both shipped into all three artifacts until later reviews caught them.
Law tokens were attached to the fix's design (parse-dont-validate) beyond what the code proved, and the agent later had to walk that back in a doc comment.
